extracted.intended_audience: Applicants, registered proprietors, third parties requesting searches, and DPMA examining staff handling Section 7 utility model searches
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for conducting and reporting searches under section 7 of the German Utility Model Act (Gebrauchsmuster) at the DPMA, covering who may request a search, procedural handling, search scope, and required contents and format of the search report. Applies to utility model applications and registered utility models in Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a search request
rubrics_metrics.description: The request may be made by the applicant, the registered proprietor and by any other party (section 7 (2) sentence 1 of the Utility Model Act). The request must be filed in writing (section 7 (2) sentence 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone without residence/principal place/establishment in Germany must appoint a patent attorney or lawyer entitled/authorised in DPMA/Federal Patent Court/civil cases concerning the utility model (section 7 (2) sentence 3 in conjunction with section 28 (1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment requirement and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee as prescribed by the Patent Costs Act shall be paid together with the request; if the fee is not paid at all, not in full or not within the time limit, the request shall be deemed withdrawn pursuant to section 6 (2) of the Patent Costs Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an earlier search request exists, a later request is deemed not filed and the fee paid shall be refunded (section 7 (4) in conjunction with section 43 (4) of the Patent Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-search rule per application
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the framework of the procedure according to section 7 of the Utility Model Act, each application shall be searched only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a search request has already been received, later requests shall be deemed not to have been filed (section 7 (4) sentence 1). The date of the earlier request is communicated to the later filer and fee refunded if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and communication of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt of the search request shall be published in the Patent Gazette; however, publication shall not take place before registration of the utility model (section 7 (3) sentence 1). If a third party has filed the request, receipt of the request shall also be communicated to the applicant or to the registered proprietor (section 7 (3) sentence 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a third party's request is found ineffective after communication to the applicant/registered proprietor, this shall be communicated to the applicant/registered proprietor and the third party (section 7 (5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity check and file transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: The search request filed shall be checked for validity. After establishment of the validity of the search request, the file shall be transmitted to the examining section competent for the main class to carry out the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The competent unit shall also arrange for communication to the applicant/registered proprietor and for publication (subject to registration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of competent examining section and class handling
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of the file, the examining section shall check whether it is competent; if not, it shall take immediate action to determine the examining section competent for the main class. The competent examining section shall be responsible for carrying out the search and, to the extent required, add any missing related classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All classification units used must be indicated in the search report (see Search report A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and pace of processing; accelerated processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches shall be performed without undue delay in the chronological order of receipt. Examining sections are advised to carry out searches so results are available before expiry of the priority year if possible. Upon a well‑founded request for accelerated processing, the order of requests may be adjusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for accelerated processing is well founded if regular processing would likely cause considerable disadvantages to the requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party state‑of‑the‑art submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person is authorised to provide information on the state of the art to the DPMA to be taken into consideration in assessing protectability (section 7 (3) sentence 3). Such information shall be communicated promptly to the applicant or the registered proprietor and, when a search procedure is pending, to the examining section too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This state of the art shall be included in the search report if it is deemed relevant by the competent examining section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter of the search — claims-based
rubrics_metrics.description: The search shall cover the subject matter to be protected according to the claims. The description and the drawings shall be considered for the interpretation of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are several versions of the claims, the search shall be based on the version last filed that the competent examining section considers to be admissible within the meaning of section 4 (5) of the Utility Model Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search purpose — preliminarily assess protectability
rubrics_metrics.description: The search shall determine the state of the art in a way that it can be used as a basis for preliminarily assessing the protectability of the invention in respect of which an application has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each application will be searched only once; the examining section shall make use of existing technical tools and sources where useful and justified, and shall always consider the state of the art mentioned by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of tools, sources and prior searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Examining sections shall make use of existing technical tools and sources of information if useful and where effort seems justified; this shall always include consideration of the state of the art mentioned by the applicant. It shall be checked to the extent possible whether previous search results are available in other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When database searches are used, a report about the complete procedure (selected databases and search terms) must be prepared and included electronically (see database search reporting entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicating determined state of the art per claim
rubrics_metrics.description: For each claim that does not only contain commonly known facts, the determined state of the art has to be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The documents indicated by the applicant or registered proprietor shall be taken into consideration by the competent examining section; if needed, the applicant/registered proprietor shall be requested to provide the documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting prior art for broad main claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If, due to the broadness of the main claim, the state of the art to be cited is too broad, the state of the art shall be selected which comes closest to the subject matter of the invention taking into account restricting features of the dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description and drawings shall be considered for claim interpretation when selecting closest prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing patent documents, it is sufficient if one member of each patent family is taken into account unless there are reasons to believe that essential differences as to substance will be found in individual family members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose representative family member unless substantive differences are suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough but not excessive search — termination criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The search shall be thorough but not excessive. The search shall be terminated if, in the course of the search, the examiner sees that an unjustified amount of work would be necessary to achieve a modest improvement of the already obtained search result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise proportionality between effort and incremental value of additional searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date for the search
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference date for the search shall be the filing date rather than a priority date claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For split‑off utility model applications under section 5 (1), the filing date of the patent application serving as the basis shall be relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of subsequently published and international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequently published patent applications and utility models with an earlier priority must be cited if available as state of the art at the time the search is carried out. International (PCT) applications where the DPMA is the designated office and European patent applications where Germany has been designated have to be mentioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may be necessary to take into consideration a grace period under section 3 (1) sentence 3 of the Utility Model Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database search reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of database searches, a report about the complete procedure of the search containing the selected databases as well as the search terms used shall be prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report shall be included as an electronic document in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling deficiencies preventing search
rubrics_metrics.description: If a search on the subject matter or parts of it cannot be carried out due to deficiencies in the documents filed, this shall be included in the search report indicating the respective claims and giving the reasons why the search was not carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clearly which claims were affected and why; do not perform ungrounded examination-like assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search report — required classification (A)
rubrics_metrics.description: The search report shall contain classification of the subject matter under the International Patent Classification (IPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All classification units used must be indicated, even if it was not possible to determine the state of the art in that class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search report — fields and tools used (B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The search report shall indicate the fields and tools used for the search (e.g. databases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All classification units and search tools used for the search shall be indicated, even if no pertinent state of the art was found in a given class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search report — results with claim references (C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The determined state of the art with reference to the respective numbers of the claims, if applicable, with explanations and references to relevant passages and drawings, shall be listed (table if necessary). No reference to claims shall be made in case of state of the art which cannot be attributed to any of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications are to be cited according to the two-letter country code pursuant to WIPO ST.3; include numbers and kind codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation categories / relevance indicators (WIPO ST.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The categories (relevance indicators) of the determined state of the art shall be indicated in capital letters pursuant to WIPO Standard ST.14. Codes defined include: X, Y, A, O, P, T, E, D, L with specified meanings (e.g. X = citation which, taken alone, challenges novelty or inventive step; Y = citation relevant in combination to challenge inventive step; A = background; O = oral disclosure/prior use; P = state of the art published during priority interval; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact ST.14 codes and apply the definitions provided; mark documents accordingly in the results listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑patent literature citation and archival handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-patent literature such as book or periodical passages is to be cited so as to ascertain unequivocally the work and passages concerned. Non‑patent literature whose printing/copying may be restricted may not be integrated into the electronic case file for copyright reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record such documents in the DPMA’s non-patent literature archive and include full bibliographic data and archive identification numbers in the electronic case file; restricted NPL must be transmitted separately by post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and correctness disclaimer in report (D)
rubrics_metrics.description: The search report shall contain a notice that completeness of the state of the art ascertained and correctness of the categories given cannot be guaranteed (section 7 (6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explicit disclaimer in the search report text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter not searched — notice and prohibition of examination-like statements (E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject matter of claims under section 2 is not protectable or a search cannot be carried out for other reasons, a notice stating this and the reasons shall be included in the search report. Further references suggesting an examination-like assessment of the subject matter are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly indicate which claim items were not searched and why; avoid making patentability judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and public inspection of search report
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant/registered proprietor and the party who filed the request shall receive the determined state of the art together with the search report. Cited non-patent literature is available to the public only within the scope of online file inspection; restricted NPL is transmitted separately by post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper transmission channels and observe copyright constraints when providing copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of serious mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after publication of the reference to the search report in the Patent Gazette, a serious mistake relating to the cited state of the art (e.g. wrong reference) is discovered, a rectification shall be published in the Patent Gazette and the parties concerned notified. If the wrong document was dispatched, the correct one shall be forwarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take corrective publication and notification steps promptly when material errors are found.
